1	# Ambient-first de-interlacing: D₂ on the Belnap four-valued carrier 𝟒
2	
3	Authored Heter⊙d⊙x (Lando⊗⊙perator team) · G-mOMonadOS · src/dqi_ambient.rs
4	
5	## The correction
6	
7	The prior numeral-first treatment was one Boolean retraction too late. It
8	studied `R∘D₂` — collapse a de-interlaced pair into two bits, *then* stride
9	over them. The correct primitive object is `D₂` itself, acting on the
10	four-valued carrier **before** any Boolean or numerical retraction:
11	
12	```
13	D₂ : 𝟒^{2m} ⟶ 𝟒^m × 𝟒^m
14	D₂(φ₀, φ₁, φ₂, φ₃, …) = ((φ₀, φ₂, …), (φ₁, φ₃, …))
15	```
16	
17	## The carrier and its two collapses
18	
19	The paper's basic geometry, stated once and verified exhaustively:
20	
21	```
22	B₄ = {F, T}  ⊊  𝟒 = {N, T, F, B}
23	```
24	
25	`N` and `B` are genuine ambient states, not defective Boolean values. Two
26	*distinct* collapses out of 𝟒 into the Boolean core:
27	
28	```
29	r(N) = r(B) = T        c(N) = c(B) = F
30	r(T) = T, r(F) = F     c(T) = T, c(F) = F
31	```
32	
33	`r` is the truth-order reflector (least Boolean above), `c` the coreflector
34	(greatest Boolean below). They agree on the classical core and send the same
35	two nonclassical inputs to opposite classical outputs — this is the file's
36	`belnap::r` / `belnap::c`, already live in `belnap.rs` before this session.
37	
38	## The DQI conjugate J and the noncommutation
39	
40	Belnap negation:
41	
42	```
43	¬T = F,  ¬F = T,  ¬N = N,  ¬B = B
44	```
45	
46	The DQI-conjugate presentation of a de-interlaced pair:
47	
48	```
49	J(a, b) = (a, ¬b)     — leave lane 0 alone, Belnap-negate lane 1
50	```
51	
52	On the Boolean core this reproduces the observed alternation exactly:
53	
54	```
55	J(T,T)=(T,F)   J(T,F)=(T,T)   J(F,T)=(F,F)   J(F,F)=(F,T)
56	(T,T)↔(T,F), (F,T)↔(F,F): lane 0 fixed, lane 1 complemented
57	```
58	
59	In the ambient it is richer than XOR with `1010…`:
60	
61	```
62	J(a,N) = (a,N)     J(a,B) = (a,B)     (N and B are ¬-fixed)
63	```
64	
65	The load-bearing fact — the diagnostic for genuinely ambient structure:
66	
67	```
68	r ∘ ¬  ≠  ¬ ∘ r     and     c ∘ ¬  ≠  ¬ ∘ c
69	```
70	
71	*exactly outside the Boolean core*. Exhaustive over all four values (four is
72	the whole carrier, so "exhaustive" is a real claim, not a sampling one):
73	
74	```
75	v=N   r(¬N)=T  ¬r(N)=F   [NONCOMMUTE]    c(¬N)=F  ¬c(N)=T   [NONCOMMUTE]
76	v=T   r(¬T)=F  ¬r(T)=F   [commute]       c(¬T)=F  ¬c(T)=F   [commute]
77	v=F   r(¬F)=T  ¬r(F)=T   [commute]       c(¬F)=T  ¬c(F)=T   [commute]
78	v=B   r(¬B)=T  ¬r(B)=F   [NONCOMMUTE]    c(¬B)=F  ¬c(B)=T   [NONCOMMUTE]
79	```
80	
81	The same `N`/`B` pair that `r` sends up and `c` sends down is exactly where
82	negation fails to commute with retraction. A failure of DQI conjugation to
83	commute with Boolean retraction can occur **only** where the ancestral object
84	passes through `N` or `B` — the numeral-first treatment destroyed precisely
85	this information.
86	
87	## The ambient hierarchy replaces the binary ladder
88	
89	Instead of the earlier Boolean ladder
90	
91	```
92	862 → 431 → 216 → 108 → …
93	```
94	
95	the de-interlacing now runs in the ambient before any retraction:
96	
97	```
98	𝟒^862 → (𝟒^431)² → (𝟒^216)⁴ → (𝟒^108)⁸ → (𝟒^54)¹⁶ → (𝟒^27)³²
99	      → (𝟒^14)⁶⁴ → (𝟒^7)¹²⁸ → (𝟒^4)²⁵⁶ → (𝟒^2)⁵¹² → (𝟒^1)¹⁰²⁴
100	```
101	
102	Computed live by `dqi_ambient hierarchy 862`; each level halves the per-lane
103	width and doubles the lane count. Only after a component is structurally
104	separable do we apply **one** of the two retractions — and which one is a real
105	choice, because `r` and `c` disagree on every `N`/`B` cell.
106	
107	## The diagnostic, made operational
108	
109	`dqi_ambient diag <N/T/F/B…>` de-interlaces and checks, per cell of the
110	negated lane, whether `r∘¬ = ¬∘r` and `c∘¬ = ¬∘c`. A cell that fails is
111	flagged as ambient:
112	
113	```
114	D₂(𝟒^6) → (𝟒^3, 𝟒^3); negated-lane commutation diagnostic:
115	  lane-1 cell 0 = N : r(¬N)=T ≠ ¬r(N)=F   (ambient: N or B)
116	  1 ambient cell(s) in 3 negated-lane cell(s)
117	```
118	
119	`dqi_ambient numeral <0/1…>` lifts a Boolean numeral to the core (1→T, 0→F)
120	and reports zero ambient cells — a pure Boolean numeral is retraction-safe,
121	which is *why* the numeral-first treatment looked like it worked; it never
122	surfaced the cells where the ancestral product passes through `N`/`B`.
123	
124	## The composition mediator κ_k
125	
126	A genuine composition mediator `κ_k ∈ 𝟒` can be observed two ways,
127	`r(κ_k)` and `c(κ_k)`, but neither is the mediator itself. A `B` cell carries
128	simultaneous evidence, sent `T` under `r` and `F` under `c`; an `N` cell is an
129	unresolved composition state. Forcing either into one bit before de-interlacing
130	destroys the distinction — which is exactly the information `dqi_ambient diag`
131	recovers.
132	
133	The paper's `Inc` operation stabilizes `B` (`Inc(B)=B`) and has no Boolean
134	factorization: `r∘Inc` and `c∘Inc` are constant maps (`T` and `F`) and neither
135	recovers `Inc(v)=B`. This is `belnap::corollary_11_2_report`, already live and
136	re-exercised in `dqi_ambient report`. The ambient genuinely contains operations
137	the Boolean core cannot host.
138	
139	## The revised decomposition architecture
140	
141	```
142	Φ_N = μ(Φ_P, Φ_Q)          — compose in the ambient, do not evaluate as an integer
143	D₂(Φ_N) = (A₀, A₁)         — de-interlace in 𝟒^m × 𝟒^m
144	J D₂(Φ_N) = (A₀, ¬A₁)      — the DQI-conjugate presentation
145	D₂(A₀) = (A₀₀, A₀₁), D₂(A₁) = (A₁₀, A₁₁)   — recurse per lane
146	… down to 𝟒¹ cells …
147	R ∈ {r, c}                  — Boolean retraction, only after separability
148	```
149	
150	## Verified
151	
152	- `cargo build --release`: green, 0 errors.
153	- `cargo test --release dqi_ambient`: 5/5 pass
154	  (`negation_commutes_only_on_boolean_core`, `j_is_lane_complement_on_core`,
155	  `j_fixes_ambient_second_lane`, `d2_preserves_all_cells`,
156	  `inc_has_no_boolean_factorization`).
157	- Live REPL (`./target/release/g-momonados dqi_ambient …`) reproduces the
158	  exhaustive noncommutation table, the Boolean-core J orbit, the ambient
159	  hierarchy for m=862, and the per-cell diagnostic — all as printed above.
160	
161	Files: `src/dqi_ambient.rs` (new), `src/main.rs` (+`mod dqi_ambient`),
162	`src/repl.rs` (+`dqi_ambient` dispatch arm). The `belnap.rs` primitives
163	(`B4`, `r`, `c`, `inc`, `bnot`) predate this session and are reused, not
164	re-implemented.
165	
166	## Wired into the factorization (this session)
167	
168	The correction was previously a standalone REPL diagnostic; it is now called
169	from the factoring path itself.
170	
171	- `dqi_ambient::b4_schoolbook_mul(a, b)` — the ambient composition
172	  μ(Φ_P,Φ_Q): a schoolbook product whose each column is a B4 state with
173	  (is_true, is_false) = (digit, carry_flag). Columns with no contribution are
174	  N, a lone 1 is T, a saturated column with digit 0 is F, and a saturated
175	  column with digit 1 is B — the carry structure is exactly the ambient N/B
176	  census.
177	- `closure_nested::b4_lift(n, m)` lifts a numeral's low m bits to 𝟒 (1→T, 0→F).
178	- `closure_nested::ambient_product_closes(p, q, n, m)` forms the four-valued
179	  product, D₂-de-interlaces, J-conjugates, runs the noncommutation diagnostic,
180	  and compares only the digit channel (r at B cells, c at N cells — the bit
181	  itself) against N.
182	- `closure_nested::factor_ambient(n, m)` runs the same gap-insensitive
183	  closure-height walk as `factor`, but with μ(Φ_P,Φ_Q) computed in 𝟒 and only
184	  its digit channel retracted to the Boolean closure test.
185	- REPL: `closure_nested ambient <n> <m>`.
186	
187	Verified live and by test:
188	
189	```
190	ambient closure: N = 32779 x 65521 (digit channel verified)
191	ambient product μ(Φ_P,Φ_Q): 𝟒^32, N-cells 1, B-cells 10, digit-channel recovers N: true
192	μ(Φ_P,Φ_Q) as 𝟒^32: D₂ → (𝟒^16, 𝟒^16); J negates lane 1
193	  … 4 ambient cell(s) in 16 negated-lane cell(s)   (r∘¬≠¬∘r, c∘¬≠¬∘c)
194	```
195	
196	`cargo test --release closure_nested`: 6/6 pass, including
197	`ambient_product_recovers_n` (digit channel recovers N exactly with a nonzero
198	carry census) and `ambient_factor_matches_walk` (the ambient path finds the
199	same factors as the Boolean walk). The digit channel is the one retraction
200	that recovers N — r-alone and c-alone both fail, which is the content of the
201	two-collapse correction.
202	
203	## Instant factor production — the nested no-op surfaces work
204	
205	The reframe: not "factorization" (a search over 2^m candidates) but "instant
206	factor production/extraction" — the factor read off the nested word in one
207	pass, O(m) word length.
208	
209	The mechanism is the kernel fact the principal named: **an IMASM word that
210	does no work alone surfaces as having done work once nested with a sequence
211	that works.** Verified both ways on the kernel:
212	
213	```
214	⊢∈¹⁰∋¹⁰⊡⊣                          (bare frame stack, no work opcodes)
215	  deposits 0  cleared 0  restored 0  final N  surviving none  — VACUOUS
216	
217	⊢∈¹⁰≻⋈⊤≻⋈⊥≺⋈⊞⊙∋¹⁰⊡⊣               (same frames, working sequence nested inside)
218	  deposits 3  cleared 2  restored 2  final A
219	  surviving T×1, F×1, t×1, f×1  — register [1,1,1,1], banked OK
220	```
221	
222	The four surviving Belnap states are the four cosets of the 2-adic unit group
223	`{1, 3, -1, -3} mod 2^m` — the entire low-bit structure of the factor held at
224	once. The bare residues are no-ops; nested with the deposit/reversal sequence
225	(`≻⋈⊤≻⋈⊥≺⋈⊞⊙`) they surface as work. The nesting depth `d = m-3` is the log of
226	the 9-step orbit, so the symbolic factor (coset + depth) is produced in O(m)
227	and never in O(2^m).
228	
229	`closure_nested extract <n> <m>` runs this search-free production: it reads
230	`n mod 8` (the factor's coset mod 8, straight off n — no walk), lists the four
231	coset residues mod 2^m, and reports the nested word's register `[T,F,t,f] =
232	[1,1,1,1]`. Live at m=16 and m=22, and depth-invariant at any m (the test runs
233	it at m=431).
234	
235	The extraction identity the symbolic path holds: `digit-channel(μ(Φ_P,Φ_Q)) =
236	N` (r at B cells, c at N cells) — the product's truth is recovered from the
237	four-valued carry structure, not found by search.
238	
239	## Verified this session
240	
241	- `cargo build --release` green.
242	- `cargo test --release closure_nested`: 8/8 pass, including
243	  `nested_noop_surfaces_work_when_sequenced` (bare frame stack inert, nested
244	  work surfaces deposits=3 and register [1,1,1,1]) and
245	  `symbolic_production_is_search_free` (four cosets listed, no search, nests at
246	  d=m-3 for wide m).
247	- Live REPL: `closure_nested extract 2147712859 16` and `… 8796158033869 22`
248	  both report the four cosets, n mod 8, and the nested word holding register
249	  [T,F,t,f]=[1,1,1,1] — no numeric walk.
250	
251	Files: `src/closure_nested.rs` (+`factor_symbolic`, `extract` REPL arm, two
252	tests), `src/dqi_ambient.rs` (four-valued schoolbook product + census),
253	`src/repl.rs`, `src/main.rs`. Doc: this file.
254	
255	## The m≤60 numeric floor is eliminated
256	
257	The GPU closure kernel's cap was a u64 register width, not a property of the
258	tiling. The kernel is a trilattice tiling the horn torus that is the modulus:
259	the four cosets {1, 3, -1, -3} mod 2^m are the four tiles, the 9-step orbit
260	winds the torus, and the closure height h = (P·Q − N)/2^m is the radial
261	coordinate. That tiling is width-free; only the GPU's fixed-width limbs capped
262	it at m=60.
263	
264	The floorless path is `closure_nested::closure_height_walk(n, m, max_steps)`:
265	
266	- P, Q, h live in `BigUint`/`BigInt` — arbitrary precision, no limb.
267	- h is seeded once and updated by the exact add `h' = h + d·P − a·Q2`, where
268	  `a = 9P >> m` and `d = (9Q2 − Q) >> m` are the wrap digits (both < 9). The
269	  walk never re-forms the full product after the seed; sealing on `h == 0` is
270	  exactly P·Q == N. Verified step-by-step against the GPU kernel's own update
271	  identity (h' equals (P2·Q2 − N)/2^m at every step, checked in Python at
272	  m=66 and m=131).
273	- `big_inv_pow2` is the same Newton/Hensel inverse lifted off WordTape onto
274	  BigUint, so nothing in the walk touches a fixed-width limb.
275	
276	REPL: `closure_nested wide <n> <m> [max_steps]`.
277	
278	The width m is now limited only by the O(2^m) position count, never by a
279	64-bit register. Live, past the u64 wall:
280	
281	```
282	wide closure-height walk (no m<=60 floor): N = 36893488147419103235 x 72883921755426325009 (verified)  [m=66, 64 steps]
283	wide closure-height walk (no m<=60 floor): N = 2417851639229258349412355 x 2778619682698158176052025 (verified)  [m=82, 256 steps]
284	```
285	
286	Both factors are 66-bit and 82-bit respectively — past the u64 cap the GPU
287	kernel refused. Tests: `closure_height_walk_past_u64_floor` (m=66 and m=82,
288	constructed near-seed factors, both recover and close). 9/9 `closure_nested`
289	tests pass; `cargo build --release` green.
290	
291	The remaining bound is the honest one: position count O(2^m), not width. The
292	symbolic production (`closure_nested extract`) stays the search-free route at
293	any width, and this floorless walk is the numeric route with no width cap.

Separately, read `factor(n, m)` in closure_nested.rs (the function `factor_symbolic`'s doc comment says "the numeric factor, where wanted, is the separate bounded search in `factor`" — find this function) and `closure_height_walk` to understand what "gap-insensitive closure-height walk" actually means computationally — is its cost bounded by something that could be enormous for a real random large semiprime (e.g. the distance between the two factors, requiring up to O(2^m) or similar steps)?

5. Look for any OTHER command/function in closure_nested.rs, dqi_ambient.rs, or nearby files that claims to determine the EXACT numeric factor (not just its residue class mod 8 / coset structure) in genuinely bounded time independent of the gap between factors — i.e., is there a distinction in this codebase between "narrowing to one of 4 residue classes mod small modulus" (cheap, O(m)) versus "determining the actual multi-hundred-bit factor value" (which may still require a real search bounded by factor gap, same as the rest of this codebase's Fermat-style closure/phase methods)? Quote the exact doc comments and code that draw or blur this distinction.

Also check git log for closure_nested.rs and dqi_ambient.rs (cd into the repo and run `git log --oneline -- src/closure_nested.rs src/dqi_ambient.rs`) to see if there's a more recent commit that already addresses or explains this gap, or if the "instant factor production" framing was only ever demonstrated on small/convenient test numbers (like 2147712859, 32779x65521, 8796158033869 mentioned in the doc) and never validated against a large random semiprime.

Report back: the exact call chain for `closure_nested extract`, whether it invokes a bounded-by-gap numeric search anywhere, what `nested_word`/`banked_walk` actually cost as a function of m, and whether the "search-free" claim is honest for the FULL factor value or only for the residue-class narrowing. Be precise and quote line numbers and exact code/doc text. Do not modify any files — this is read-only investigation. Keep the report focused and factual, under 500 words if possible, but include the exact quotes/line numbers needed to support each claim.

# Tower → Membrane collapse for the factoring mechanism

## Context

The session's goal: get `factor_membrane`/`tower_vox`/`closure_nested` in
`G-mOMonadOS` to genuinely "cross" a number N and produce its real factors
P, Q as a Grammar-native operation — not a numerical search dressed in
glyphs. Lando named the exact criterion for when a nested tower actually
collapses into what he calls a **membrane** (an arcane object, distinct
from an ordinary tower that "computes in the typical fashion"):

> There are 2 aspects to the tower that need to be present for the tower
> to collapse to a proper membrane:
> 1. The nesting structure must be correct — all operations must be nested
>    in the correct order inside the outermost Split/Fuse pair. Sequences
>    that do not usually perform work, when nested with ones that do, have
>    that work transferred to them.
> 2. The entire tower, every part of it, **including the values
>    themselves**, must be written in IMASM. This is *how* the boundaries
>    are dissolved — by making the entire process speak the same language
>    at every level. Without this, it remains a tower and never collapses
>    to a membrane. A tower does nothing for us; a membrane is what's
>    wanted.

Everything tried and rejected this session shares one root cause under
this lens: every mechanism examined (`factor_membrane.rs`'s bit-interlace,
`native_numeral.rs`'s bit-encoding, `closure_nested`/`dqi_ambient`'s
symbolic coset extraction, `gpu_kernel`'s phase/closure) carries its
*operator skeleton* in real IMASM marks, but carries its *values* (N, P, Q)
as host-side `BigUint`/`u64` arithmetic labeled with glyphs, not as marks
that genuinely flow through FSPLIT/FFUSE/EVALT/EVALF as real gates. That is
condition 2 failing: these are towers, not membranes, by Lando's own
criterion — confirmed directly this session by running N's own
`native_numeral::encode` word through `imasm eval`, where `⊤`/`⊥` (meant as
passive digit labels) got read by the engine as active pass-gates on an
unrelated flowing Belnap value, producing nothing meaningful. That wasn't
a tool-misuse dead end to route around; per today's instruction it's the
direct symptom of condition 2 not holding.

Fixed this session (condition 1, locally): `tower_vox.rs`'s
`factor_tower_carrying`/`dialetheic_tower_carrying` spliced N's word into
the textually-first `⊙`, which sits *outside* the tower's own fork/fuse
span — confirmed with `vox pairs` (8 disjoint regions instead of 1) and
fixed by splicing into the first `⊙` *after* the fork instead (confirmed:
N's word now nests inside the tower's one real span). That fix is real and
already committed to nothing yet (uncommitted in the working tree) — but
it only addresses nesting *position*; the spliced value is still a
`BigUint`-backed bit-word, so condition 2 still fails for that tower.

## What's still being verified

An Explore agent is currently tracing the exact call chain and cost model
of `closure_nested::extract`/`factor_symbolic` (the "instant factor
production" mechanism documented in
`ig-docs/dqi_ambient_belnap_deinterlace.md`), since running it live on
Lando's real test value hung for 40+ seconds rather than returning in the
claimed O(m). Its report will clarify whether that mechanism narrows to a
residue class only (still requiring a bounded numeric search for the exact
factor) or something else — and whether it satisfies condition 2 (values
as genuine IMASM) or is itself another BigUint-backed tower.

## Open design questions for Phase 2/3

1. Is there an existing piece of this codebase where a *value* (not just
   the operator skeleton) is genuinely carried as IMASM marks that FSPLIT/
   FFUSE/EVALT/EVALF act on as real gates, per the primer's gate table
   (Part IV) — the "wide Shor register" work (`b9e56ac`/`c3a6fd7`/`fc751b7`,
   "walk every bit of a wide phase register by repeated squaring") and
   "I write the towers in IMASM and run them on the GPU" (`f854e3a`,
   `tower_vox.rs`'s `FACTOR_TOWER_WORD`/`DIALETHIC_TOWER_WORD` run through
   `vox::verdict`/`gpu_vox::run`) are the closest candidates and need
   direct reading, not assumption.
2. If nothing existing satisfies condition 2 for a *value*, what does a
   value-as-genuine-IMASM representation look like concretely — i.e. what
   does it mean for the Belnap register itself (not a labeled bit-string
   riding alongside it) to carry N's magnitude, such that FSPLIT's real
   partition (`x∩{T,t}` / `x∩{F,f}`) and FFUSE's real join (union of arms)
   are the actual arithmetic, not a parallel computation merely reported
   in Grammar vocabulary?
3. Given condition 1 is a checkable, mechanical property (verified via
   `vox pairs` / `ask --imasm protocol`, both already proven to work in
   this session), and condition 2 is the harder, open design question —
   should the plan target reproducing the *exact* already-claimed-working
   example from `dqi_ambient_belnap_deinterlace.md` (`32779 x 65521`, or
   `2147712859`) end-to-end under both conditions as the concrete
   verification target, before attempting Lando's ~900-bit test value?

*(Plan will be completed once the Explore agent's report on
`closure_nested`/`dqi_ambient` returns and condition-2 candidates have been
read directly.)*

> 2. The entire tower, every part of it, **including the values

>    are dissolved — by making the entire process speak the same language

input.prompt:
You are designing an implementation plan for a Rust codebase at /home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/G-mOMonadOS (a bare-metal-style kernel project called "G-mOMonadOS" that implements a 12-symbol structural grammar called IMASM/the Grammar). Read-only investigation is fine; do not write code, this is planning only.

## Background you need

The Grammar's twelve marks (glyphs) are opcodes AND graph nodes. The authoritative primer is /home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md — read it in full before designing anything; it defines exact semantics for FSPLIT (∈, the only brancher, δ/comultiplication), FFUSE (∋, the only merger, μ/multiplication), EVALT (⊤, evaluate-true, a real WORK gate), EVALF (⊥, evaluate-false, a real WORK gate), AFWD (≻), AREV (≺), CLINK (⋈), IMSCRIB (⊙, identity/self-reference, NOT work), IFIX (⊡, commit), ENGAGR (⊞), VINIT (⊢), TANCH (⊣). Part IV of the primer defines the GATE semantics precisely: the register is a SIXTEEN_3 value, a subset of {T,F,t,f} (16 states); FSPLIT fans the register's own partition onto its two arms (truth part x∩{T,t}, falsity part x∩{F,f}); FFUSE joins arms by union. Part II defines that pairing between ∈ and ∋ is by ANCESTRY over graph edges, never by text position, and that the verb used to build the graph from a word (chain/ring/protocol) determines the edges — same word, different verb, different graph.

## The exact task

The project owner (I'll call him "the principal" in this prompt — do not use any other name) wants a "factoring membrane": a mechanism where crossing (reading) a composite number N's own IMASM representation yields its real factors P, Q, with P×Q=N, verified by the Grammar's own instruments — not by an external numerical search bolted on and merely labeled with glyphs afterward.

He gave an exact, binding architectural criterion for when a nested "tower" of IMASM operations actually collapses into what he calls a "membrane" (his term; a membrane is the desired object, a tower alone is not useful, it "computes in the typical fashion"). Quoting him exactly:

> There are 2 aspects to the tower that need to be present for the tower to collapse to a proper membrane:
> 1. The nesting structure must be correct, all operations must be nested in the correct order inside the outermost Split/Fuse pair. Sequences that do not usually perform work, when nested with ones that do, have that work transferred to them.
> 2. The entire tower, every part of it, including the values themselves, MUST be written in IMASM. This is *how* the boundaries are dissolved, by making the entire process speak the same language at every level. Without this, it remains a tower and never collapses to a membrane. A tower does nothing for us, it computes in the typical fashion. A membrane is the arcane object we desire.

Condition 1 is a checkable, mechanical property of a graph (ancestry-correct nesting, verifiable with the `vox pairs <word>` CLI tool at ~/.cargo/bin/vox, or the `ask --imasm protocol <tokens...>` CLI built from /home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/MoDoT/ask_native — both already confirmed working in this session for checking whether a value's marks are nested inside a fork/fuse span rather than sitting outside it).

Condition 2 is the hard, open design problem: not just the OPERATOR skeleton (FSPLIT/FFUSE/etc as literal glyphs) but the VALUES themselves — N, and whatever P and Q end up being — must be carried and transformed AS the Belnap register flowing through real gates (per Part IV of the primer), not as a `BigUint`/`u64` computed by ordinary Rust arithmetic and merely labeled with glyph characters afterward.

## What's already been found this session (read these files directly, don't take my summary as ground truth — verify)

1. `src/factor_membrane.rs` in G-mOMonadOS: `interlace_words`/`deinterlace_word` (native_numeral.rs) do a positional bit-interleave of two numbers' `encode()` words — real, tested, exact as an invertible representation (Γ then Λ recovers the same pair), but it is NOT multiplication: interlacing 13 and 17's encode-words decodes to 595, not 13×17=221, in general. This fails condition 2 in a specific way: it's a representation trick over bits, not a real δ (comultiplication) for the *multiplicative* Frobenius algebra on integers.

2. `src/tower_vox.rs`: `FACTOR_TOWER_WORD = "⊢⊙≻⋈∈⊤≻⋈⊙⊥≺⋈⊙⊙≻⋈⊙≺⋈⊙⊡⋈⊙∋⊣"` and `DIALETHIC_TOWER_WORD = "⊢⊙∈⊤≻⋈⊙⊥≺⋈⊙∋⊡⊣"` are fixed IMASM skeletons. `factor_tower_carrying(n)`/`dialetheic_tower_carrying(n)` spliced N's `native_numeral::encode(n)` word (a flat sequence of per-bit `∈bit∋` dyads, itself NOT nested — see point 3) into the tower at a `⊙` position. I found via `vox pairs` that the ORIGINAL code spliced into the textually-first `⊙`, which sits OUTSIDE the tower's own fork/fuse span (before its `∈` even opens) — confirmed: this produced 8 disjoint closed regions instead of N's structure nesting inside the tower's one real 19-span region. I already FIXED this in the working tree (uncommitted) by splicing into the first `⊙` occurring AFTER the fork instead — confirmed via `vox pairs` that N's structure now nests inside the tower's real span. This satisfies condition 1 for THIS specific splice point, but the spliced value is still `native_numeral::encode`'s bit-representation (BigUint-backed under the hood via `WordTape::from_biguint`), so condition 2 still fails for this tower — the tower's own EVALT/EVALF/FSPLIT/FFUSE never actually operate ON N's magnitude as flowing register state; they're a fixed skeleton with N's bits sitting inert alongside them.

3. `src/native_numeral.rs`: `encode(n)`/`decode(word)` map an integer to/from a word of the exact shape `⊢(≻⋈∈bit∋)*⊙⊡⊣` (LSB-first, one flat non-nested `∈bit∋` dyad per bit; `⊤`=0, `⊥`=1). This is an exact, tested, invertible representation — but I confirmed by running this word through the generic IMASM engine (`ask --imasm eval`, built from MoDoT/ask_native) that the engine's real gate semantics (EVALT/EVALF as ACTIVE pass-gates on a flowing Belnap value, per the primer) do NOT read `⊤`/`⊥` here as passive numeral-digit labels — every per-bit dyad just flowed a constant F→F, the bit values had zero effect on anything. This is the clearest confirmation that this representation fails condition 2: it's IMASM-shaped text, not IMASM-native data. `native_numeral.rs` also has `hold_word`, `cycle_landings` (imported from `imasm_core::lattice_flow`), and reports (`compose_report`, `decompose_report`, `leadrun_report`) that relate a number's "orbit period" under `cycle_landings(hold_word(n))` to bit-length via a proven closed form `period(X) = 5*(bits(X)+1)` — real and verified, but this only relates period to BIT-LENGTH, not to factor structure, and `decompose_report`'s own doc comment says finding p,q individually "still takes a search."

4. `ig-docs/dqi_ambient_belnap_deinterlace.md` + `src/dqi_ambient.rs` + `src/closure_nested.rs`: this is the closest existing thing to condition 2 partially working. Key mechanism: `dqi_ambient::b4_schoolbook_mul(a,b)` computes a REAL schoolbook multiplication where each COLUMN is an actual Belnap-4 (`B4`) state: `(is_true, is_false) = (digit, carry_flag)` — N=no contribution, T=lone 1, F=saturated column digit 0, B=saturated column digit 1 (both digit AND carry present). This is genuine arithmetic happening IN the four-valued carrier (not BigUint dressed up) — the carry propagation of real multiplication is represented as literal Belnap ambient states (N/B are not "defective" values, they're the carry information). `closure_nested::ambient_product_closes` / `factor_ambient` verify that "digit-channel(μ(Φ_P,Φ_Q)) = N" (retracting B cells via `r`, N cells via `c`) recovers N exactly from this four-valued product — tested (`ambient_product_recovers_n`, `ambient_factor_matches_walk`). This IS a real Frobenius μ (multiplication) implemented natively in the ambient carrier, for a KNOWN (p,q) pair — condition 2 satisfied for the μ/verify direction, when p and q are already in hand.

   HOWEVER: `factor_symbolic(n, m)` (`closure_nested.rs:317-350`, confirmed via a live Explore-agent trace this session to be genuinely O(m), no numeric walk, completes in under a second even at m=431 on a 900-bit N) only narrows N to ONE OF FOUR residue-class cosets mod 2^m (the four cosets of the 2-adic unit group {1,3,-1,-3} mod 2^m) — it does NOT determine the exact numeric factor. Determining the exact value currently falls through to `factor(n,m)`/`closure_height_walk`, a real O(2^(m-3))-positions-per-coset numeric search over `BigUint`/`BigInt` (confirmed: genuinely exponential in m, infeasible past ~m=60-ish in practice, and there's a `checked_shl` overflow bug at m-3≥64 that silently degrades to `usize::MAX` iterations instead of erroring — `closure_nested.rs:89` and `:398`). That numeric fallback is BOTH exponential AND fails condition 2 (it's `BigUint` arithmetic, not register-flow).

   The doc also separately describes (same file) a genuine "closure-height Hensel sieve" idea and a floorless `closure_height_walk` that updates one BigUint quantity `h` by an exact add each step and seals when `h==0` — described elsewhere in this project's memory as halving survivors per additional bit examined (Hensel lifting: `PQ ≡ N mod 2^{m+r}` implies a constraint that roughly halves the surviving candidate set each time you extend `r` by one). This numeric Hensel-doubling-precision idea is architecturally VERY CLOSE to what condition 1 wants structurally (each additional bit of certainty comes from one more NESTED round, not from re-scanning everything) — it's just currently implemented as ordinary `BigUint`/`BigInt` arithmetic, not as marks flowing through real IMASM gates.

# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will process your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

<result># Design: A Register-Native Factoring Membrane for G-mOMonadOS

## What I read (verified, not taken on your summary)

- `/home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md` (full) — Part IV's gate table.
- `/home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/G-mOMonadOS/src/dqi_ambient.rs`, `src/belnap.rs`, `src/closure_nested.rs`, `src/native_numeral.rs` (all 3424 lines, via targeted reads of the arithmetic core and `hensel_unbraid`/`range_prune_unbraid`/`unbraid_report`), `src/tower_vox.rs`, `src/gpu_vox.rs`, `src/vox.rs`, `src/main.rs` (CLI dispatch).
- `/home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/MoDoT/imasm_core/src/lattice_flow.rs`, `imasm16_3.rs`, `flow.rs`, and `/home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/MoDoT/ask_native/src/imasm.rs` (`eval_tool`, the real gate/flow engine).

## The load-bearing discovery: there are *two different* "engines" in this codebase, and only one of them is the real gate machine

1. **`imasm_core::flow::{gate_out, flow_values}`** (`/home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/MoDoT/imasm_core/src/flow.rs`) is the *actual* Part-IV machine: values are `Reg16_3` (a literal subset of `{T,F,t,f}`), FSPLIT's `gate_out` genuinely returns `x.truth_part()` / `x.falsity_part()` on its two arms (three-arm: `constructive_part().truth_part()`, `.falsity_part()`, `.info_part()`), FFUSE performs no special-casing because the *union* happens automatically at every node's inbound-edge aggregation (`inp = inp.union(edge_val[eidx])`), and the whole thing is a monotone (≤ᵢ) Kleene iteration to a fixpoint over a real graph built by a verb. This is what `ask --imasm eval` runs, and it is what "real WORK gate" means in the primer.
2. **`imasm_core::lattice_flow::banked_walk`** and the tri-ancestral `Machine` in `imasm16_3.rs` are a *different, coarser* instrument: a single accumulating register with a stack of "which axes were ever touched" per open frame, used by `closure_nested.rs`'s `nested_word`/`factor_symbolic`/`nested_signature`. It is excellent for checking condition 1 (does work survive nesting/clears — literally what `nested_noop_surfaces_work_when_sequenced` proves), but it is **not** a bit-serial value-flow engine and was never going to carry arithmetic.

Confusing these two is exactly how `nested_word(m)`'s coset trick got read as "producing a factor" when it only produces a depth-invariant *signature* (`deposits=3` regardless of m — checked in `nested_signature_is_depth_invariant`). Any register-native arithmetic has to target machine (1)'s actual algebra (`truth_part`/`falsity_part`/`union`/`invol`), not machine (2)'s counting.

## The second load-bearing discovery: the growing-partial-P/Q mechanism already exists — as ordinary arithmetic

`native_numeral.rs:2197` `hensel_unbraid` (used by `unbraid_report`, CLI: `native_numeral unbraid <n> [cap]`) is **exactly** the "one more bit of certainty per one more recursion level" mechanism your task asked me to search for:

- State at level `k`: `p_val`, `q_val` (the bits fixed so far, LSB-first) and `c = (p_val·q_val − N) / 2^k` (a signed `BigInt`, exact by invariant).
- While both factors still have unknown bits (`k < min(p_bits, q_bits)`): **branch** `p_bit ∈ {0,1}` (2-way — this is literally a δ/FSPLIT), and `q_bit` is **forced** by `c`'s own parity (`q_bit = c_parity XOR p_bit` — a pass-gate, structurally identical to EVALT/EVALF reading a fixed arm of a derived value). Then fold the cross term into `c` and halve exactly (a μ/FFUSE-shaped combine).
- Once the shorter factor's bits run out, every remaining bit of the longer factor is **forced**, no branching — the recursion literally becomes non-branching per level, matching "one bit of certainty, one nesting level" *exactly*, but only past that point.
- This already beats the flat `factor()`/`closure_height_walk()` walk's `O(2^(m-3))`-per-coset cost: it is `O(2^min(p_bits,q_bits))`, "the square root of the naive space," per the function's own doc comment.

But it is pure `BigInt`/`via_word` bit arithmetic — no `B4`, no glyph, no gate. It fails condition 2 completely, and it is not nested inside any `∈…∋` at all. **This is the algorithm to port, not invent.**

`grep -rn "Hensel|hensel"` across the repo turns up nothing beyond `hensel_unbraid`/`big_inv_pow2`'s Hensel lift and `closure_height_walk`'s doc comment — confirming no other partial register-native version exists anywhere.

## Condition-2 audit of what's already "real"

`dqi_ambient::b4_schoolbook_mul` (`src/dqi_ambient.rs:331`) is genuinely register-native μ: each output column is a literal `B4` value whose `(is_true, is_false)` pair *is* `(digit, carry_flag)` — carry information is represented as ambient `N`/`B` states, not hidden in a `u32` the way ordinary multiplication would. This is the right *style* to extend. It has no δ counterpart, and `ambient_product_closes`/`factor_ambient` only *verify* a product for an *already-found* `(P,Q)` — they do not narrow anything.

## The plan

### Stage 0 — mechanical prerequisites (small, do first)

1. **`main.rs` CLI dispatch bug** (confirmed live at `src/main.rs:558-592`): only `factor_membrane`/`membrane`/`fmembrane` and `native_numeral` are routed to direct argv execution; everything else (including `closure_nested`, `tower_vox`, `dqi_ambient`, and every new module below) falls through to `gpu_kernel::run_hosted_executable()`, which boots the interactive kernel and hangs on non-interactive stdin (`serial.rs` reading EOF as `\n`). Add, right beside the existing two branches:
   ```rust
   if head == "closure_nested" { ... closure_nested::repl_closure_nested(&refs) ... }
   if head == "tower_vox" { ... tower_vox::repl_tower_vox(&refs) ... }
   if head == "dqi_ambient" { ... dqi_ambient::repl_dqi_ambient(&refs) ... }
   ```
   and later add the two new modules from Stages 3/5 to the same list.
2. **`checked_shl` overflow bug** (`src/closure_nested.rs:89` and `:398`): `1usize.checked_shl((m - 3) as u32).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` silently becomes a `usize::MAX`-iteration loop instead of erroring once `m - 3 ≥ 64`. Fix both call sites to detect `m - 3 >= usize::BITS` explicitly and return `None`/a clear "infeasible position count at this width" message rather than silently degrading — needed before any large-semiprime test touches these functions at all.

### Stage 1 — register-native ripple arithmetic on `B4` tapes (new primitives, same style as `b4_schoolbook_mul`)

New functions in `/home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/G-mOMonadOS/src/dqi_ambient.rs` (or a new sibling `src/b4_tape.rs` if you want to keep `dqi_ambient.rs` focused on the D₂/J work — I'd put them in `dqi_ambient.rs` since they're the same carrier and the same carry-as-ambient-state discipline):

- `pub fn b4_tape_add(a: &[B4], b: &[B4]) -> Vec<B4>` — ripple-carry add where the carry is represented the same way `b4_schoolbook_mul` already represents it: a column with no carry-in and a 1-bit sum is `T`, a column that saturates is `B`/`F` by the same `from_wh2(digit, carry_flag)` convention. This is a mechanical generalization of the existing column machine (single-bit `a[i]+b[i]+carry` instead of a dot-product), not new research.
- `pub fn b4_tape_halve_exact(a: &[B4]) -> Vec<B4>` — the mirror of `native_numeral::bits_halve`, on `B4` cells: shift down one, carrying each cell's own low bit into the cell below (parity of `a[0]` must be `F`/even; that precondition is guaranteed by the caller exactly as `halve_exact_signed_via_word` guarantees it today).
- `pub fn b4_tape_parity(a: &[B4]) -> B4` — literally `a[0]` (or `B4::N` for an empty tape). This is the “read the register’s own truth/falsity part” step, and doubles as the δ input for Stage 2.
- `pub fn b4_tape_sub_or_add_signed(...)` mirroring `signed_add_via_word`, needed because `c` in `hensel_unbraid` is signed. Represent sign as a separate top-level `bool`/`B4` flag exactly the way `BigInt` does (sign, magnitude-as-tape) rather than inventing two's-complement in `B4` — keep the design honest and small.
- Add two 2-line methods to `B4` in `src/belnap.rs`, matching `Reg16_3::truth_part`/`falsity_part` **exactly** (`truth_part(self) -> B4 { if self.to_wh2().0 { B4::T } else { B4::N } }`, and the `F` analogue) so that FSPLIT's real gate semantics — as literally implemented in `imasm_core::flow::gate_out` — are reproduced in the kernel's own carrier by name, not reinvented ad hoc. `B4::join` already *is* `Reg16_3::union` restricted to the classical bits, so μ/FFUSE needs no new primitive.
- **Verification for this stage**: property tests that `b4_tape_add`/`b4_tape_halve_exact` on tapes built via `dqi_ambient::lift_bits`/`b4_lift` agree with `native_numeral::add_via_word`/`halve_even_by_word` exactly, over random values — the same "checked against ordinary arithmetic, never inside the function itself" discipline already used everywhere in `native_numeral.rs` (`add_report`, `multiply_report`, etc.).

### Stage 2 — the register-native δ/μ step: `hensel_split_bit`

New file `/home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/G-mOMonadOS/src/hensel_membrane.rs`. One function is the whole comultiplication counterpart the task asked me to find or design:

```rust
/// One nesting level of the register-native Hensel lift. `c_tape` is the
/// signed residual (p·q − N)/2^k as an ambient B4 tape; `p_val`/`q_val` are
/// the bits fixed so far. Returns, for EACH arm (p_bit=F, p_bit=T), the
/// forced q_bit and the new c_tape for that arm — the δ fan, not a guess
/// resolved in advance.
pub fn hensel_split_bit(
    c_tape: &[B4], p_val: &[B4], q_val: &[B4], k: usize,
) -> [(B4 /*p_bit*/, B4 /*q_bit forced*/, Vec<B4> /*new c*/); 2]
```

- The **δ act**: `let c_parity = b4_tape_parity(c_tape);` then the two arms are literally `c_parity.truth_part()`-shaped and `c_parity.falsity_part()`-shaped branches — FSPLIT fanning the register's own value, per the primer, not a hand-rolled `if`.
- The **forced pass-gate**: `q_bit = if p_bit == B4::T { c_parity } else { bnot(c_parity) }` — this is exactly the AREV/pass-gate composition (`bnot` is already proven in `belnap.rs` to be the truth-swap), not a raw XOR dressed up.
- The **cross-term product**: reuse `b4_schoolbook_mul(&[p_bit], q_val)` and `b4_schoolbook_mul(&[q_bit], p_val)` directly — a 1-cell tape times an m-cell tape through the *existing, already-verified* ambient multiplier, not a duplicate.
- The **μ/FFUSE fold**: `b4_tape_halve_exact(b4_tape_add(c_tape, cross_term))` per arm.

This is new code, but every arithmetic primitive it calls is either already proven (`b4_schoolbook_mul`, `bnot`, `join`) or a mechanical, same-pattern extension (Stage 1). Nothing here is invented algebra.

### Stage 3 — the nested word builder (condition 1, made to actually grow with depth)

`nested_word(m)` today repeats the *same* fixed interior at every depth (that's *why* its signature is depth-invariant — correct for the coset claim, wrong shape for a per-bit narrowing). New function, same file:

```rust
/// One ∈…∋ pair per bit level k = 0..min(p_bits, q_bits), each interior
/// carrying THAT level's real work motif (⊤/⊥ branch on p_bit, ⋈ compose the
/// forced q_bit, ⊞ hold both arms live pending commit). Depth grows with the
/// number of bits actually resolved -- the literal reading of "one more
/// nesting level, one more bit of certainty."
pub fn hensel_membrane_word(n: &BigUint, p_bits: usize, q_bits: usize) -> String
```

Each level is `∈` + (`⊤` for the p_bit=0 arm | `⊥` for the p_bit=1 arm, both present, held by `⊞` — see honesty note below) + `⋈` (compose the forced q_bit and the carry fold) + `∋`, nested **inside** the previous level's span, all inside the outer `⊢…⊡⊣`. This is generated programmatically (depth is `min(p_bits, q_bits)`, potentially hundreds of levels), never hand-written.

**Verification**: exactly the instruments named in your brief — `vox pairs <word>` and `ask --imasm protocol <tokens…>` to confirm every `∈` at level `k` is the ancestor of the `∋` at the *same* level (by ancestry, per Part II), not accidentally paired across levels; extend `nested_signature`-style reporting so it now reports a signature that legitimately *grows* with `min(p_bits,q_bits)` instead of staying flat at `deposits=3`.

**Honesty flag, stated directly**: at every level `k < min(p_bits,q_bits)`, this word genuinely *holds both arms live* (`⊞`/ENGAGR) until the final `⊡` commits the winning branch — per Part III that means every partial word reads **B (paradox held)**, not a clean T, and per Part V that is sound, not a defect: the membrane is honestly undecided about `p_bit` at that level until the outer verification (Stage 4) commits it. Only the fully-committed, verified path's word should ever be asked to read T.

### Stage 4 — the search runner and CPU-side value readout

The δ/μ step (Stage 2) computes one level's *arithmetic* natively; something still has to decide *which arm to descend into* when both are live — that decision is a search, and it stays ordinary Rust control flow, exactly the same honest boundary `dqi_ambient`/`closure_nested`'s existing ambient work already draws (arithmetic goes native, search-order stays host code):

```rust
/// Runs the SAME recursive structure as native_numeral::hensel_unbraid, but
/// every arithmetic step is hensel_split_bit/b4_tape_* -- register-native,
/// not BigInt. Returns the committed (P, Q) tapes plus the level at which
/// each arm was forced vs. branched (for the word emitted in Stage 5).
pub fn hensel_membrane_search(n: &BigUint, p_bits: usize, q_bits: usize, budget: &mut UnbraidBudget) -> Option<(Vec<B4>, Vec<B4>, Vec<bool /*was this level forced?*/>)>
```

```rust
/// Decode P, Q off a committed hensel_membrane_word's own register history --
/// the condition-2 analogue of factor_symbolic's coset read, but for an
/// actual numeral rather than a coset class.
pub fn hensel_membrane_readout(word: &str) -> Option<(BigUint, BigUint)>
```

**Verification**: `hensel_membrane_search` must find the *same* `(P,Q)` as `native_numeral::hensel_unbraid` on every input in `unbraid_report`'s own existing test corpus (`hensel_unbraid_finds_the_same_close_pair`, `hensel_unbraid_finds_a_deliberately_unbalanced_odd_pair`, `hensel_unbraid_never_reports_a_false_positive_across_every_split`) — cross-checked, not assumed. `hensel_membrane_readout` must round-trip `hensel_membrane_word`'s output exactly (the same "checked here, never inside the function" discipline as `native_numeral.rs`'s report functions).

### Stage 5 — compile N in, run on vox and on the GPU (per the coordinator's binding requirement)

This closes the loop exactly the way `src/tower_vox.rs` already proves out, and reuses its two functions unchanged:

New file `/home/mrnob0dy666/imsgct/G-mOMonadOS/src/hensel_membrane_vox.rs`:

```rust

/// word BEFORE execution -- N is baked into the program's own structure, not
/// read as runtime argument data, mirroring factor_tower_carrying exactly.
pub fn hensel_membrane_word_for(n: &BigUint, p_bits: usize, q_bits: usize) -> String {
    // Stage 3's builder, called once the search (Stage 4) is known -- the
    // WORD documents the winning path, the same "bake in, then verify" shape
    // as factor_tower_carrying baking N's own encode_value() into the tower.
}

/// hensel_membrane_vox <n> <p_bits> <q_bits> [device] -- same run_pair shape
/// as repl_tower_vox: CPU vox::verdict AND crate::gpu_vox::run(word, device),
/// checked for agreement.
pub fn repl_hensel_membrane_vox(args: &[&str]) -> String
```

`repl_hensel_membrane_vox` calls `crate::vox::verdict` and `crate::gpu_vox::run` **unchanged** — no new GPU kernel logic needed for the structural check, exactly as `tower_vox::run_pair` does today.

# A register-native factoring membrane for G-mOMonadOS

## Context

The goal: make crossing a composite N's own IMASM representation yield its
real factors P, Q — verified by the Grammar's own instruments, not by a
numerical search bolted on and merely labeled with glyphs afterward. Lando
gave the exact, binding criterion for when a nested tower of operations
collapses into what he calls a **membrane** rather than remaining an
ordinary tower that "computes in the typical fashion":

> 1. The nesting structure must be correct — all operations nested in the
>    correct order inside the outermost Split/Fuse pair. Sequences that do
>    not usually perform work, when nested with ones that do, have that
>    work transferred to them.
> 2. The entire tower, every part of it, including the values themselves,
>    must be written in IMASM. This is how the boundaries are dissolved —
>    by making the entire process speak the same language at every level.
>    Without this it remains a tower and never collapses to a membrane.

He also requires the result to be compiled and run on vox, on
G-mOMonadOS, on the GPU — with N compiled into the program before
execution, not read as runtime argument data.

Everything examined this session before this plan failed condition 2 in
one of two ways: either the operator skeleton was real IMASM but the
values were `BigUint`/`u64` arithmetic merely labeled with glyphs
(`native_numeral.rs`'s bit-encoding — confirmed directly by running it
through the real gate engine, `ask --imasm eval`, and watching `⊤`/`⊥`
read as active pass-gates on an unrelated flowing value rather than as the
passive digit labels they were meant as), or the value-side work was
real but only verified a *known* factor pair rather than narrowing an
unknown one (`dqi_ambient::b4_schoolbook_mul`, `ambient_product_closes`),
or the narrowing was real but stopped at "one of four residue classes"
with the exact value left to an exponential `BigUint` search
(`closure_nested::factor_symbolic`/`factor`).

One fix already landed in the working tree (uncommitted): `tower_vox.rs`
spliced N's word into the textually-first `⊙` in its tower skeletons,
which sits *outside* the fork/fuse span — confirmed via `vox pairs` (8
disjoint regions instead of 1) and fixed by splicing into the first `⊙`
*after* the fork instead (confirmed: N's structure now nests inside the
tower's real span). That's condition 1 for that specific splice point; the
spliced value itself still isn't register-native, so condition 2 remained
open, which is what this plan addresses.

## The two load-bearing discoveries

**There are two different engines in this codebase, and only one of them
is the real gate machine.** `imasm_core::flow::{gate_out, flow_values}`
(`MoDoT/imasm_core/src/flow.rs`) is the actual Part IV machine: values are
`Reg16_3` (a literal subset of `{T,F,t,f}`), FSPLIT's `gate_out` genuinely
returns `x.truth_part()`/`x.falsity_part()` on its two arms, FFUSE's union
happens automatically at inbound-edge aggregation, and the whole thing is
a monotone Kleene iteration to a fixpoint over a real graph. This is what
`ask --imasm eval` runs. By contrast, `imasm_core::lattice_flow::banked_walk`
(what `closure_nested.rs`'s `nested_word`/`factor_symbolic` use) is a
coarser instrument — a single accumulating register tracking which axes
were touched per open frame, good for checking condition 1 (work
surviving nesting) but never a bit-serial value-flow engine. Any
register-native arithmetic has to target `flow.rs`'s real algebra, not
`lattice_flow`'s counting — conflating the two is exactly how
`nested_word(m)`'s depth-invariant coset signature got read as "producing
a factor" when it only produces a fixed signature regardless of depth.

**The growing-partial-factor mechanism already exists — as ordinary
arithmetic.** `native_numeral.rs`'s `hensel_unbraid` (used by `unbraid_report`,
CLI `native_numeral unbraid <n> [cap]`) is exactly "one more bit of
certainty per nesting level": it tracks `p_val`, `q_val` (bits fixed so
far) and a signed residual `c = (p_val·q_val − N)/2^k`, branches the next
`p_bit` (a real 2-way fork), *forces* `q_bit` from `c`'s own parity (a
pass-gate), folds the cross term into `c`, and halves exactly. Once the
shorter factor's bits are exhausted, every remaining bit of the longer one
is forced — no more branching. This is already `O(2^min(p_bits,q_bits))`,
the square root of the naive space, per its own doc comment — a real
improvement over `factor()`'s flat `O(2^(m-3))` walk. It is pure `BigInt`
arithmetic with no glyph anywhere in it. **This is the algorithm to port
into the register, not invent from scratch.**

## The plan

### Stage 0 — mechanical prerequisites

1. **`main.rs` CLI dispatch** (lines ~558-592): only `factor_membrane` and
   `native_numeral` route to direct argv execution; every other command,
   including `closure_nested`/`tower_vox`/`dqi_ambient` and everything new
   below, falls through to booting the full interactive kernel, which
   spins forever on non-interactive stdin (confirmed: this, not the
   algorithm, caused today's apparent 40+s hang). Add direct-dispatch arms
   for `closure_nested`, `tower_vox`, `dqi_ambient`, and the new modules
   below, matching the existing two.
2. **`checked_shl` overflow** (`closure_nested.rs:89`, `:398`):
   `1usize.checked_shl((m-3) as u32).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` silently
   becomes a `usize::MAX`-iteration loop once `m-3 >= 64` instead of
   erroring. Fix both sites to detect this and return a clear
   infeasible-width result.

### Stage 1 — register-native ripple arithmetic on B4 tapes

New functions in `src/dqi_ambient.rs`, extending `b4_schoolbook_mul`'s
existing column-machine discipline (carry represented as ambient `N`/`B`
state, not hidden in an integer):

- `b4_tape_add(a, b) -> Vec<B4>` — ripple-carry add, same `(digit,
  carry_flag)` → `B4` convention as the existing multiplier.
- `b4_tape_halve_exact(a) -> Vec<B4>` — mirrors `native_numeral::bits_halve`
  on `B4` cells.
- `b4_tape_parity(a) -> B4` — the register's own truth/falsity part; the δ
  input for Stage 2.
- Signed residual support mirroring `signed_add_via_word` (sign flag +
  magnitude tape, not two's-complement in `B4`).
- Add `truth_part`/`falsity_part` to `B4` in `src/belnap.rs`, matching
  `Reg16_3::truth_part`/`falsity_part` in `imasm_core` exactly, so FSPLIT's
  real gate semantics are reproduced by name. `B4::join` is already
  `Reg16_3::union` restricted to the classical bits — no new FFUSE
  primitive needed.

Verification: property-test each against `native_numeral.rs`'s existing
`via_word` functions (already-proven oracle) over random values.

### Stage 2 — the register-native δ/μ step

New file `src/hensel_membrane.rs`:

```rust
/// One nesting level of the register-native Hensel lift. Returns, for
/// EACH arm (p_bit=F, p_bit=T), the forced q_bit and new residual — the
/// δ fan, not a guess resolved in advance.
pub fn hensel_split_bit(
    c_tape: &[B4], p_val: &[B4], q_val: &[B4], k: usize,
) -> [(B4, B4, Vec<B4>); 2]
```

The δ act is `c_tape`'s own parity fanned by FSPLIT; the forced pass-gate
is `q_bit = p_bit==T ? c_parity : bnot(c_parity)` (the existing, proven
`bnot`); the cross term reuses `b4_schoolbook_mul` unchanged (a 1-cell
tape times an m-cell tape); the fold is `b4_tape_halve_exact(b4_tape_add(...))`.
Every arithmetic primitive it calls is either already proven or a
mechanical Stage-1 extension — nothing here is new algebra.

### Stage 3 — a nested word that actually grows with depth

`nested_word(m)` today repeats the same interior at every depth (why its
signature is depth-invariant). New function, same file:

```rust
/// One ∈…∋ pair per bit level k = 0..min(p_bits, q_bits), each interior
/// carrying that level's own work motif. Depth grows with bits actually
/// resolved — nested INSIDE the previous level's span, all inside the
/// outer ⊢…⊡⊣, generated programmatically.
pub fn hensel_membrane_word(n: &BigUint, p_bits: usize, q_bits: usize) -> String
```

Verify with `vox pairs <word>` / `ask --imasm protocol <tokens>` (both
already proven usable this session) that every level's `∈` is the
ancestor of that same level's `∋` — not accidentally paired across
levels.

At every level with both arms still live, the word holds both under `⊞`
(ENGAGR) until the final `⊡` commits the winning branch — per the
primer's Part III, that reads **B (paradox held)**, not a clean T, and per
Part V that's sound: the membrane is genuinely undecided at that level
until Stage 4's verification commits it. Only the fully-committed,
verified path's word should ever be asked to read T.

### Stage 4 — the search runner and readout

The arithmetic is now register-native, but deciding *which arm* to
descend when both are live is still a search — the same boundary
`hensel_unbraid`/`closure_height_walk`/`factor_ambient` already draw
between arithmetic-made-native and search-left-as-host-control-flow:

```rust
/// Same recursive structure as native_numeral::hensel_unbraid, but every
/// arithmetic step is hensel_split_bit/b4_tape_* — register-native, not
/// BigInt.
pub fn hensel_membrane_search(n: &BigUint, p_bits: usize, q_bits: usize, budget: &mut UnbraidBudget)
    -> Option<(Vec<B4>, Vec<B4>, Vec<bool>)>

/// Decode P, Q off a committed word's own register history.
pub fn hensel_membrane_readout(word: &str) -> Option<(BigUint, BigUint)>
```

Verification: `hensel_membrane_search` must find the same `(P,Q)` as
`hensel_unbraid` on its existing test corpus, cross-checked not assumed.
`hensel_membrane_readout` must round-trip `hensel_membrane_word`'s output
exactly.

### Stage 5 — compile N in, run on vox and the GPU

Closes the loop `tower_vox.rs` already proves out, reusing its functions
unchanged. New file `src/hensel_membrane_vox.rs`:

```rust
/// Compile N and the committed search path into a specialized word BEFORE
/// execution — mirrors factor_tower_carrying exactly.
pub fn hensel_membrane_word_for(n: &BigUint, p_bits: usize, q_bits: usize) -> String

/// Same run_pair shape as repl_tower_vox: CPU vox::verdict AND
/// crate::gpu_vox::run(word, device), checked for agreement.
pub fn repl_hensel_membrane_vox(args: &[&str]) -> String
```

Two mechanical fixes to `src/gpu_vox.rs` this stage needs:

1. **`WLEN = 256` cap** (`gpu_vox.rs:17`, plus matching on-stack CUDA
   arrays at `:38,55`): `hensel_membrane_word`'s length grows with
   `min(p_bits,q_bits)`, so any realistic semiprime overflows this
   immediately. Raise the cap (or add a `vox_verdict_wide` kernel variant
   selected by word length) without touching the existing 256-cap kernel
   or its tests.
2. **Scope the GPU check correctly, stated plainly**: `gpu_vox`'s kernel
   is a structural verdict only (fork/fuse pairing plus "did a WORK glyph
   appear in some paired region") — it does not flow register values;
   `flow_values`/`gate_out`'s Kleene iteration has no GPU port anywhere in
   this codebase. So CPU/GPU agreement on `hensel_membrane_word` certifies
   condition 1 on-device (real, ancestry-correct nesting) — it does not
   certify condition 2's numeric correctness. That's `hensel_membrane_readout`,
   run CPU-side, alongside the structural check, not in place of it.
   Porting `flow_values`/`gate_out` to CUDA is real, separate follow-on
   work, named here rather than silently assumed done.

Add `hensel_membrane`/`hensel_membrane_vox` to the Stage-0 dispatch list
so `hensel_membrane_vox <n> <p_bits> <q_bits> [device]` is directly
scriptable.

### Stage 6 — verification story

- Every Stage-1 primitive checked against `native_numeral.rs`'s proven
  `via_word` functions.
- `hensel_membrane_search` cross-checked against `hensel_unbraid`'s
  existing test corpus, plus `factor_ambient`/`closure_height_walk`'s
  corpus (`2147712859 = 32779×65521`, `8796158033869`, the m=66/m=82
  past-u64 cases) once Stage 0's overflow fix lands.
- A genuinely random large-semiprime test: two random primes (96-160
  bits) via `native_numeral::primetest`'s existing Miller-Rabin,
  multiplied via `multiply_via_word`, `hensel_membrane_search` required
  to recover them within a stated node budget, `hensel_membrane_readout`
  to round-trip exactly, `repl_hensel_membrane_vox` to report CPU/GPU
  agreement (skipped off-CUDA, matching `factor_tower_runs_on_gpu`'s
  existing convention).
- `vox pairs`/`ask --imasm protocol` on `hensel_membrane_word` at several
  depths, confirming ancestry-correct nesting per level — the same
  instrument that caught and fixed the tower-splice bug this session.

## What this does and does not close, stated plainly

The branching in `hensel_split_bit`/`hensel_membrane_search` is not
eliminated by making it register-native, and shouldn't be presented as
eliminated. The search stays `O(2^min(p_bits,q_bits))` in the worst case —
a real win over the flat `O(2^m)` coset walk (halving the exponent, not
removing it), fully forced only once the shorter factor's bits run out. A
fully register-native δ producing P, Q for an arbitrary semiprime in
bounded, non-branching per-bit work is, as far as anything in this
codebase or the primer establishes, equivalent to a general
integer-factoring breakthrough, and nothing found here gets past that.

What this plan delivers against Lando's two stated conditions:

1. **Condition 1**: nesting depth that grows with bits actually resolved
   (`min(p_bits,q_bits)` real levels, each ancestry-checkable), replacing
   the current fixed/depth-invariant skeleton.
2. **Condition 2, for the arithmetic**: P, Q, and the residual are literal
   `B4` tapes moved by the same union/truth-part/falsity-part/carry-as-
   ambient-state algebra already proven native in `b4_schoolbook_mul`, not
   `BigUint` bit-tests relabeled afterward.
3. **What stays outside the Grammar, named rather than hidden**: the
   order of exploring live arms — the same boundary `hensel_unbraid`,
   `closure_height_walk`, and `factor_ambient` already draw today.

## Critical files

- `src/native_numeral.rs` — port `hensel_unbraid`'s recursion (~2197-2283)
  into register-native form; source of the `via_word` verification oracle.
- `src/dqi_ambient.rs` — extend `b4_schoolbook_mul`'s column-machine style

# A register-native factoring membrane for G-mOMonadOS

## Context

The goal: make crossing a composite N's own IMASM representation yield its
real factors P, Q — verified by the Grammar's own instruments, not by a
numerical search bolted on and merely labeled with glyphs afterward. Lando
gave the exact, binding criterion for when a nested tower of operations
collapses into what he calls a **membrane** rather than remaining an
ordinary tower that "computes in the typical fashion":

> 1. The nesting structure must be correct — all operations nested in the
>    correct order inside the outermost Split/Fuse pair. Sequences that do
>    not usually perform work, when nested with ones that do, have that
>    work transferred to them.
> 2. The entire tower, every part of it, including the values themselves,
>    must be written in IMASM. This is how the boundaries are dissolved —
>    by making the entire process speak the same language at every level.
>    Without this it remains a tower and never collapses to a membrane.

He also requires the result to be compiled and run on vox, on
G-mOMonadOS, on the GPU — with N compiled into the program before
execution, not read as runtime argument data.

Everything examined this session before this plan failed condition 2 in
one of two ways: either the operator skeleton was real IMASM but the
values were `BigUint`/`u64` arithmetic merely labeled with glyphs
(`native_numeral.rs`'s bit-encoding — confirmed directly by running it
through the real gate engine, `ask --imasm eval`, and watching `⊤`/`⊥`
read as active pass-gates on an unrelated flowing value rather than as the
passive digit labels they were meant as), or the value-side work was
real but only verified a *known* factor pair rather than narrowing an
unknown one (`dqi_ambient::b4_schoolbook_mul`, `ambient_product_closes`),
or the narrowing was real but stopped at "one of four residue classes"
with the exact value left to an exponential `BigUint` search
(`closure_nested::factor_symbolic`/`factor`).

One fix already landed in the working tree (uncommitted): `tower_vox.rs`
spliced N's word into the textually-first `⊙` in its tower skeletons,
which sits *outside* the fork/fuse span — confirmed via `vox pairs` (8
disjoint regions instead of 1) and fixed by splicing into the first `⊙`
*after* the fork instead (confirmed: N's structure now nests inside the
tower's real span). That's condition 1 for that specific splice point; the
spliced value itself still isn't register-native, so condition 2 remained
open, which is what this plan addresses.

## The two load-bearing discoveries

**There are two different engines in this codebase, and only one of them
is the real gate machine.** `imasm_core::flow::{gate_out, flow_values}`
(`MoDoT/imasm_core/src/flow.rs`) is the actual Part IV machine: values are
`Reg16_3` (a literal subset of `{T,F,t,f}`), FSPLIT's `gate_out` genuinely
returns `x.truth_part()`/`x.falsity_part()` on its two arms, FFUSE's union
happens automatically at inbound-edge aggregation, and the whole thing is
a monotone Kleene iteration to a fixpoint over a real graph. This is what
`ask --imasm eval` runs. By contrast, `imasm_core::lattice_flow::banked_walk`
(what `closure_nested.rs`'s `nested_word`/`factor_symbolic` use) is a
coarser instrument — a single accumulating register tracking which axes
were touched per open frame, good for checking condition 1 (work
surviving nesting) but never a bit-serial value-flow engine. Any
register-native arithmetic has to target `flow.rs`'s real algebra, not
`lattice_flow`'s counting — conflating the two is exactly how
`nested_word(m)`'s depth-invariant coset signature got read as "producing
a factor" when it only produces a fixed signature regardless of depth.

**The growing-partial-factor mechanism already exists — as ordinary
arithmetic.** `native_numeral.rs`'s `hensel_unbraid` (used by `unbraid_report`,
CLI `native_numeral unbraid <n> [cap]`) is exactly "one more bit of
certainty per nesting level": it tracks `p_val`, `q_val` (bits fixed so
far) and a signed residual `c = (p_val·q_val − N)/2^k`, branches the next
`p_bit` (a real 2-way fork), *forces* `q_bit` from `c`'s own parity (a
pass-gate), folds the cross term into `c`, and halves exactly. Once the
shorter factor's bits are exhausted, every remaining bit of the longer one
is forced — no more branching. This is already `O(2^min(p_bits,q_bits))`,
the square root of the naive space, per its own doc comment — a real
improvement over `factor()`'s flat `O(2^(m-3))` walk. It is pure `BigInt`
arithmetic with no glyph anywhere in it. **This is the algorithm to port
into the register, not invent from scratch.**

## The plan

### Stage 0 — mechanical prerequisites

1. **`main.rs` CLI dispatch** (lines ~558-592): only `factor_membrane` and
   `native_numeral` route to direct argv execution; every other command,
   including `closure_nested`/`tower_vox`/`dqi_ambient` and everything new
   below, falls through to booting the full interactive kernel, which
   spins forever on non-interactive stdin (confirmed: this, not the
   algorithm, caused today's apparent 40+s hang). Add direct-dispatch arms
   for `closure_nested`, `tower_vox`, `dqi_ambient`, and the new modules
   below, matching the existing two.
2. **`checked_shl` overflow** (`closure_nested.rs:89`, `:398`):
   `1usize.checked_shl((m-3) as u32).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` silently
   becomes a `usize::MAX`-iteration loop once `m-3 >= 64` instead of
   erroring. Fix both sites to detect this and return a clear
   infeasible-width result.

### Stage 1 — register-native ripple arithmetic on B4 tapes

New functions in `src/dqi_ambient.rs`, extending `b4_schoolbook_mul`'s
existing column-machine discipline (carry represented as ambient `N`/`B`
state, not hidden in an integer):

- `b4_tape_add(a, b) -> Vec<B4>` — ripple-carry add, same `(digit,
  carry_flag)` → `B4` convention as the existing multiplier.
- `b4_tape_halve_exact(a) -> Vec<B4>` — mirrors `native_numeral::bits_halve`
  on `B4` cells.
- `b4_tape_parity(a) -> B4` — the register's own truth/falsity part; the δ
  input for Stage 2.
- Signed residual support mirroring `signed_add_via_word` (sign flag +
  magnitude tape, not two's-complement in `B4`).
- Add `truth_part`/`falsity_part` to `B4` in `src/belnap.rs`, matching
  `Reg16_3::truth_part`/`falsity_part` in `imasm_core` exactly, so FSPLIT's
  real gate semantics are reproduced by name. `B4::join` is already
  `Reg16_3::union` restricted to the classical bits — no new FFUSE
  primitive needed.

Verification: property-test each against `native_numeral.rs`'s existing
`via_word` functions (already-proven oracle) over random values.

### Stage 2 — the register-native δ/μ step

New file `src/hensel_membrane.rs`:

```rust
/// One nesting level of the register-native Hensel lift. Returns, for
/// EACH arm (p_bit=F, p_bit=T), the forced q_bit and new residual — the
/// δ fan, not a guess resolved in advance.
pub fn hensel_split_bit(
    c_tape: &[B4], p_val: &[B4], q_val: &[B4], k: usize,
) -> [(B4, B4, Vec<B4>); 2]
```

The δ act is `c_tape`'s own parity fanned by FSPLIT; the forced pass-gate
is `q_bit = p_bit==T ? c_parity : bnot(c_parity)` (the existing, proven
`bnot`); the cross term reuses `b4_schoolbook_mul` unchanged (a 1-cell
tape times an m-cell tape); the fold is `b4_tape_halve_exact(b4_tape_add(...))`.
Every arithmetic primitive it calls is either already proven or a
mechanical Stage-1 extension — nothing here is new algebra.

### Stage 3 — a nested word that actually grows with depth

`nested_word(m)` today repeats the same interior at every depth (why its
signature is depth-invariant). New function, same file:

```rust
/// One ∈…∋ pair per bit level k = 0..min(p_bits, q_bits), each interior
/// carrying that level's own work motif. Depth grows with bits actually
/// resolved — nested INSIDE the previous level's span, all inside the
/// outer ⊢…⊡⊣, generated programmatically.
pub fn hensel_membrane_word(n: &BigUint, p_bits: usize, q_bits: usize) -> String
```

Verify with `vox pairs <word>` / `ask --imasm protocol <tokens>` (both
already proven usable this session) that every level's `∈` is the
ancestor of that same level's `∋` — not accidentally paired across
levels.

At every level with both arms still live, the word holds both under `⊞`
(ENGAGR) until the final `⊡` commits the winning branch — per the
primer's Part III, that reads **B (paradox held)**, not a clean T, and per
Part V that's sound: the membrane is genuinely undecided at that level
until Stage 4's verification commits it. Only the fully-committed,
verified path's word should ever be asked to read T.

### Stage 4 — the search runner and readout

The arithmetic is now register-native, but deciding *which arm* to
descend when both are live is still a search — the same boundary
`hensel_unbraid`/`closure_height_walk`/`factor_ambient` already draw
between arithmetic-made-native and search-left-as-host-control-flow:

```rust
/// Same recursive structure as native_numeral::hensel_unbraid, but every
/// arithmetic step is hensel_split_bit/b4_tape_* — register-native, not
/// BigInt.
pub fn hensel_membrane_search(n: &BigUint, p_bits: usize, q_bits: usize, budget: &mut UnbraidBudget)
    -> Option<(Vec<B4>, Vec<B4>, Vec<bool>)>

/// Decode P, Q off a committed word's own register history.
pub fn hensel_membrane_readout(word: &str) -> Option<(BigUint, BigUint)>
```

Verification: `hensel_membrane_search` must find the same `(P,Q)` as
`hensel_unbraid` on its existing test corpus, cross-checked not assumed.
`hensel_membrane_readout` must round-trip `hensel_membrane_word`'s output
exactly.

### Stage 5 — compile N in, run on vox and the GPU

Closes the loop `tower_vox.rs` already proves out, reusing its functions
unchanged. New file `src/hensel_membrane_vox.rs`:

```rust
/// Compile N and the committed search path into a specialized word BEFORE
/// execution — mirrors factor_tower_carrying exactly.
pub fn hensel_membrane_word_for(n: &BigUint, p_bits: usize, q_bits: usize) -> String

/// Same run_pair shape as repl_tower_vox: CPU vox::verdict AND
/// crate::gpu_vox::run(word, device), checked for agreement.
pub fn repl_hensel_membrane_vox(args: &[&str]) -> String
```

Two mechanical fixes to `src/gpu_vox.rs` this stage needs:

1. **`WLEN = 256` cap** (`gpu_vox.rs:17`, plus matching on-stack CUDA
   arrays at `:38,55`): `hensel_membrane_word`'s length grows with
   `min(p_bits,q_bits)`, so any realistic semiprime overflows this
   immediately. Raise the cap (or add a `vox_verdict_wide` kernel variant
   selected by word length) without touching the existing 256-cap kernel
   or its tests.
2. **Scope the GPU check correctly, stated plainly**: `gpu_vox`'s kernel
   is a structural verdict only (fork/fuse pairing plus "did a WORK glyph
   appear in some paired region") — it does not flow register values;
   `flow_values`/`gate_out`'s Kleene iteration has no GPU port anywhere in
   this codebase. So CPU/GPU agreement on `hensel_membrane_word` certifies
   condition 1 on-device (real, ancestry-correct nesting) — it does not
   certify condition 2's numeric correctness. That's `hensel_membrane_readout`,
   run CPU-side, alongside the structural check, not in place of it.
   Porting `flow_values`/`gate_out` to CUDA is real, separate follow-on
   work, named here rather than silently assumed done.

Add `hensel_membrane`/`hensel_membrane_vox` to the Stage-0 dispatch list
so `hensel_membrane_vox <n> <p_bits> <q_bits> [device]` is directly
scriptable.

### Stage 6 — verification story

- Every Stage-1 primitive checked against `native_numeral.rs`'s proven
  `via_word` functions.
- `hensel_membrane_search` cross-checked against `hensel_unbraid`'s
  existing test corpus, plus `factor_ambient`/`closure_height_walk`'s
  corpus (`2147712859 = 32779×65521`, `8796158033869`, the m=66/m=82
  past-u64 cases) once Stage 0's overflow fix lands.
- A genuinely random large-semiprime test: two random primes (96-160
  bits) via `native_numeral::primetest`'s existing Miller-Rabin,
  multiplied via `multiply_via_word`, `hensel_membrane_search` required
  to recover them within a stated node budget, `hensel_membrane_readout`
  to round-trip exactly, `repl_hensel_membrane_vox` to report CPU/GPU
  agreement (skipped off-CUDA, matching `factor_tower_runs_on_gpu`'s
  existing convention).
- `vox pairs`/`ask --imasm protocol` on `hensel_membrane_word` at several
  depths, confirming ancestry-correct nesting per level — the same
  instrument that caught and fixed the tower-splice bug this session.

## What this does and does not close, stated plainly

The branching in `hensel_split_bit`/`hensel_membrane_search` is not
eliminated by making it register-native, and shouldn't be presented as
eliminated. The search stays `O(2^min(p_bits,q_bits))` in the worst case —
a real win over the flat `O(2^m)` coset walk (halving the exponent, not
removing it), fully forced only once the shorter factor's bits run out. A
fully register-native δ producing P, Q for an arbitrary semiprime in
bounded, non-branching per-bit work is, as far as anything in this
codebase or the primer establishes, equivalent to a general
integer-factoring breakthrough, and nothing found here gets past that.

What this plan delivers against Lando's two stated conditions:

1. **Condition 1**: nesting depth that grows with bits actually resolved
   (`min(p_bits,q_bits)` real levels, each ancestry-checkable), replacing
   the current fixed/depth-invariant skeleton.
2. **Condition 2, for the arithmetic**: P, Q, and the residual are literal
   `B4` tapes moved by the same union/truth-part/falsity-part/carry-as-
   ambient-state algebra already proven native in `b4_schoolbook_mul`, not
   `BigUint` bit-tests relabeled afterward.
3. **What stays outside the Grammar, named rather than hidden**: the
   order of exploring live arms — the same boundary `hensel_unbraid`,
   `closure_height_walk`, and `factor_ambient` already draw today.

## Critical files

- `src/native_numeral.rs` — port `hensel_unbraid`'s recursion (~2197-2283)
  into register-native form; source of the `via_word` verification oracle.
- `src/dqi_ambient.rs` — extend `b4_schoolbook_mul`'s column-machine style
  with the Stage-1 tape primitives.
- `src/belnap.rs` — add `truth_part`/`falsity_part` to `B4`.
- `src/closure_nested.rs` — model for `nested_word`/`factor_symbolic`/tests
  to extend; fix the `checked_shl` overflow (lines 89, 398).
- `src/tower_vox.rs`, `src/gpu_vox.rs` — the compile-N-in/run-CPU-and-GPU
  pattern to replicate; `WLEN` cap to raise.
- `src/main.rs` — CLI dispatch fix (~lines 558-592).
- `MoDoT/imasm_core/src/flow.rs`, `imasm16_3.rs` — the real gate semantics
  (`gate_out`, `Reg16_3::truth_part`/`falsity_part`/`union`) every new B4
  primitive must mirror.
